chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), concerning

a man whose family presumed he had died or been killed, so his wife was married and his concubine was married; each of the two gave birth to a child from her husband. Then the first husband came, or the master of the concubine came, and the ruling in that matter was that the first takes his wife, for he is more entitled to her, and the master takes his concubine and her child, unless he takes willingly the price of the child.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a husband returns after his wife remarried during his presumed death?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the status of remarriage during the period of 'ghurrah' (presumed death), establishing that the original husband retains primary rights to reclaim his wife upon return, while the master keeps the concubine and child unless compensating the new husband. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the initial marital bond remains superior to the subsequent one in cases of uncertainty, ensuring family continuity and property rights are preserved according to the original contract.
